display.purpose: Editorial title pages and future display moments only; not yet applied in the product.

headline.purpose: Page titles, club names, read titles, and dialog headings.

title.purpose: Card titles, section headings, and reading-session names.

label.purpose: Short uppercase micro-headings, status labels, and metadata labels.

shadows.name: overlay-lift
shadows.purpose: Dropdowns, dialogs, popovers, and toasts only. Signals detachment from the page.

shadows.name: residual-card-softness

components.name: Primary Button

components.name: Secondary Button

components.name: Text Input

narrative.overview:
LitLoop reads as a small circulating library that happens to run itself: a parchment ground, white catalogue cards, ink-navy structure, and a single gold stamp. The library metaphor is functional rather than decorative. Books are catalogued, clubs are registered, and every read is stamped with a date and a place. The mood is warm, literary, and quietly social; the interface never performs bookishness with props.

Density is moderate and task-led. An organizer should see the live read, its meetup, and its RSVP state without hunting, while a reader should feel invited into the next gathering rather than dropped into a feed. Warmth comes from the palette, the Ethiopic-first type, the humane rounding, and real covers. Navy carries structure. Gold marks the read that is currently alive.

This system is explicitly not a generic SaaS dashboard, not corporate library software, not sepia cosplay, and not a social feed. The scheduled read outranks the metric tile, the engagement badge, and the infinite scroll.
keyCharacteristics: Parchment page ground, Paper White sheet surfaces, Ink Navy structure.
One Bookplate Gold accent, used sparingly as a stamp and a live-read signal.
Ethiopic-first humanist sans; Playfair Display held in reserve for editorial display.
Soft radius ladder (8/12/16/24px) with hairline Deckle Edge borders.
Tonal depth, not shadow-based hierarchy; shadows belong to floating layers.
Reading-first columns and a mobile bottom navigation built for thumbs.
Real book covers and club identity carry the imagery.

rules.name: The One Gold Accent Rule
rules.body: Bookplate Gold is a stamp, not a surface. Keep it under roughly 10% of any screen. Use it for the live read, small emphasis, metadata icons, and hover; never as a large background fill.

rules.name: The Parchment Ground Rule
rules.body: Pages sit on Parchment. Sheets, cards, and inputs sit on Paper White. That contrast is the primary depth cue; do not flatten it by making the page white.

rules.name: The Navy Is Structure Rule
rules.body: Ink Navy carries navigation, primary actions, and links. Body copy stays Iron Gall so the page reads as text first and chrome second.

rules.name: The Ethiopic-First Rule
rules.body: Every sans stack leads with Noto Sans Ethiopic, then Inter. Never reorder the stack or substitute a Latin-first fallback; the multilingual product depends on this order.

rules.name: The Two-Register Rule
rules.body: Interface text uses the humanist sans. Playfair Display is reserved for display and editorial moments. Never set body copy, controls, or metadata in the serif.

rules.name: The Reading Column Rule
rules.body: Club and read surfaces stay between 42rem and 56rem wide. Do not stretch a reading page to the full viewport; line length and focus matter more than filling the screen.

rules.name: The Thumb Zone Rule
rules.body: Below 640px, primary navigation lives in the fixed bottom bar. Do not duplicate the full desktop menu into a cramped top row.

rules.name: The Tonal Depth Rule
rules.body: Separate surfaces with parchment/surface contrast and hairline borders. Do not introduce shadow-based hierarchy.

rules.name: The Overlay Exception Rule
rules.body: Shadows belong only to floating layers, where they signal detachment from the page. A card is not a floating layer.

rules.name: The Soft Corner Rule
rules.body: Use the 8/12/16/24px radius ladder. Reserve full pills for search, avatars, dots, and compact tabs; do not pill every control.

rules.name: The No Hard Outline Rule
rules.body: Borders are 1px Deckle Edge. Dividers use the same hairline. Never introduce black rules or heavy structural strokes.

rules.name: The Whole-Card Link Rule
rules.body: Make entire cards clickable with a stretched link at z-10; interactive controls sit above it at z-20. Never nest a button inside an anchor.

dos: Do start pages on Parchment and place Paper White sheets on top.
Do keep Ink Navy for structure and actions, and Bookplate Gold for the live read and small emphasis.
Do set all interface text in the Ethiopic-first sans stack.
Do use the radius ladder: 8px controls, 12px small cards, 16px cards, 24px panels and dialogs, full pills for search and avatars.
Do use 1px Deckle Edge borders and tonal contrast for depth.
Do preserve the 42-56rem reading column for club and read pages.
Do give every interactive element a visible Ink Navy focus ring.
Do use real book covers and club images; keep placeholders quiet and icon-led.
Do keep uppercase for short labels and micro-headings only.
donts: Don't use pure white page backgrounds or pure black text.
Don't add shadow-based elevation to cards, panels, or sections.
Don't use gradients beyond the hero fallback and the profile banner.
Don't introduce new brand hues; success, error, and warning colors are semantic only.
Don't use sepia paper textures, script fonts, leather-and-candle imagery, or faux-vintage props.
Don't turn the product into a dashboard of metric tiles or an infinite social feed.
Don't set body copy, controls, or metadata in Playfair Display.
Don't pill every button; pills are for search, avatars, dots, and status chips.
Don't nest a button inside a card anchor; use a stretched link with controls above it.
